clue.text: Worry when given job to produce ornamental design

parts.note: to worry is to fret
a job is work

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about their task ends up carving decorative patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is decorative openwork carved in wood, a kind of ornamental pattern.

clue.text: Tried somehow to get chaps to agree in a harmful way

indicators.note: done somehow means in some unspecified fashion, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: chaps are men
to tally is to agree or match

explanation.surface: Someone tried to bring men into agreement but did damage instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Detrimental means causing damage, so the adverb describes acting harmfully.

clue.text: Short notice, fair and correct

parts.note: an ad is a notice, shortened from advertisement
fair means just

explanation.surface: Something announced at short notice is said to be fair and right.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct something is to adjust it, putting it right by small changes.

clue.text: Composer who gives others a 'distressing' experience?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ..., American composer of the Adagio for Strings
a hairdresser for men removes tresses, read whimsically as de-tressing

explanation.surface: A composer whose music leaves listeners upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressing' is split as de-tressing: cutting off locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Barber is a twentieth-century American composer; a men's hairdresser also cuts tresses.

clue.text: This bent male's running the organisation

indicators.note: running here suggests the letters move about freely and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A corrupt man is in charge of the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' signals rearranging all the letters of THIS BENT MALES; 'bent' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Establishment is the ruling group or institution, the powers that run society.

clue.text: Individual catching cold in the past

indicators.note: catching means the first word holds the second within it

parts.note: a single individual is one
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A person who caught a chill at some earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some earlier time, is a standard synonym of this adverb.

clue.text: There's little right in devil becoming a chum

indicators.note: in means the short piece is placed within the longer word

parts.note: a fiend is a devil
R is the short form of right

explanation.surface: Even a devil has a little good in him and becomes a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a close companion or pal.

clue.text: A bishop ecstatic, distracted

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
sent is old slang for transported with delight

explanation.surface: A bishop so thrilled he cannot concentrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent-minded or distracted people are mentally elsewhere.

clue.text: Celebrity sending nasty people back

indicators.note: sending back means the word is returned and read from the other end

parts.note: rats are contemptible, nasty people

explanation.surface: A famous person dismissing unpleasant hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is a famous performer or personality.

clue.text: Been playing with aunt yet to lose

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messed about with into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone playing a game with their aunt has never lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A team still without a defeat is described as undefeated.

clue.text: Pessimist, endlessly severe after reflective mood

indicators.note: after places the severe part behind the mood part
reflective here means mirrored, so the word is read backwards
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: severe means stern

explanation.surface: A gloomy person, harsh after brooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns MOOD into DOOM; 'endlessly' cuts STERN to STER.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet of gloom forever predicting disaster is a pessimist.

clue.text: Woman in garden the day before Christmas?

definitions.meaning: the first woman, in the Garden of Eden
the evening or day before a festival

explanation.surface: A woman out in the garden on Christmas Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's partner in Eden; also the day preceding a holiday.

clue.text: Many items at the auction

definitions.meaning: a great deal, as in plenty
goods offered for sale one bid at a time are ...

explanation.surface: Plenty of things for sale at an auction.
explanation.definitionFit: Means plenty, and also the numbered items sold at an auction.

clue.text: Youngster eats greens surprisingly — but no seconds whatever!

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters end up in an unexpected order
no means the named letters are removed from the words

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds; whatever means every one of them goes

explanation.surface: A young person eats vegetables, astonishingly, without any second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no seconds whatever' removes both S's from EATS GREENS, leaving EATGREEN, which 'surprisingly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A person aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.

clue.text: Son and relations hide

parts.note: kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A son and his family are hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a verb but is the noun: an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal hide is its pelt or outer covering.

clue.text: Fairy at front of hut wasted away

indicators.note: at front of places the fairy piece before the hut piece

parts.note: a peri is a fairy of Persian myth
a shed is a hut

explanation.surface: A fairy at the door of a hut, fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: To have perished is to have died or decayed, wasting away.

clue.text: Talk about one criminal at sea

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning a lawbreaker out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer who robs ships is a criminal of the seas.

clue.text: Withstand naughty sister

indicators.note: naughty means badly behaved, so the letters misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: Stand firm against a badly behaved sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand an attack is to hold out against it.

clue.text: Treat she arranged in places of entertainment

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: She organised a treat at the playhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Playhouses where drama is staged are places of entertainment.

clue.text: Landscape feature of two hectares

indicators.note: two here means the abbreviation appears twice over

parts.note: HA is the abbreviation for hectare(s)

explanation.surface: A piece of scenery covering two hectares of land.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, used on British country estates as an invisible boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken fence that keeps livestock out without spoiling the view is a garden landscaping device.

clue.text: Male to consume something from the butcher

parts.note: to consume food is to eat

explanation.surface: A man going to eat something bought at the butcher's.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher sells animal flesh for food.

clue.text: Church has a building for renting, a holiday home?

parts.note: a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A church owns a property to rent out, perhaps as a vacation retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden Alpine-style cottage, often rented for vacations, is a holiday home.

clue.text: Performer among celebrities in Germany

indicators.note: among means the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An entertainer mixing with the famous in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are found across 'celebritieS IN GERmany'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is one kind of performer.
